English: Watchtower Keep
A rudimentary frontier fortification of timber palisades and watchtowers, sheltering a small garrison and establishing basic defensive oversight.
Timber Stronghold
A reinforced wooden keep with thicker palisades, a central hall, and improved living quarters for the lord and garrison.
Stone Donjon
A tall, square stone tower (donjon) replaces wooden defenses, providing both formidable protection and a symbol of authority.
Square Keep
A large, multi-story stone keep with improved fortifications, barracks, and command quarters
French: a true bastion for noble residence and defense.

English: Round Keep
Advanced architectural techniques yield a rounded stone keep, with reinforced walls, improved arrow slits, and expanded living space for retainers.
Multi-Towered Keep
A grand fortress, boasting multiple interconnected towers, expanded walls, and layered defenses, able to withstand the fiercest sieges and house a mighty retinue.
Great Hall Fortress
A mighty fortress with a lavish great hall, vast administrative quarters, and storied halls for feasts and councils, radiating prestige and power.
Concentric Keep
An advanced keep designed with multiple layers of curtain walls and interlocking towers, maximizing defensive capability and military organization.
Royal Residence
A palatial stronghold fit for royalty, featuring vast staterooms, administrative wings, and lavish quarters that inspire awe and command loyalty.
Imperial Citadel
The ultimate castle fortress, an awe-inspiring citadel of unmatched strength, luxury, and administrative reach, heart of a true empire.
